newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Jetset says Qantas report may be true.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Jetset says Qantas report may be true.

text.p: Australian travel agency group Jetset said on Monday a newspaper report that Qantas Airways Ltd was set to buy half of Jetset from Air New Zealand Ltd could be true, but that it could not comment further.
"There could be some truth in it," Jetset Managing Director and 50 percent shareholder Isi Leibler told Reuters.
"But I can't make any further comment, because I'm subject to confidentiality agreements," Leibler said.
Earlier, The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported that Qantas was on the verge of buying the 50 percent stake for between A$15 million to A$50 million.
A Qantas spokesman said he could not comment on the report.
The Financial Review said Leibler would exercise his option to buy out Air New Zealand's stake and then onsell it to Qantas.
"According to insiders, Qantas would wind up with 50 percent of the travel distribution and technology conglomerate for anything from A$15 million to A$50 million," the Financial Review said.
Leibler would retain his half share in Jetset and management control, but would have an exit clause included allowing either partner the first option to buy the other out, it said.

"Qantas' move to secure part of Jetset, underpinning an extensive commercial deal struck last year would give the arirline a powerful stake in the wholesale and retail industry to counter the expanding Traveland busines of its rival Anset," the Financial Review said.

"It would also act as a block to Ansett's 50 percent owner, Air New Zealand, eventually consolidating the Jetset operation with that of Traveland to tie up a considerable share of the Australasian distribution market."
Qantas said last year it would buy Jetset's Tour East operations.
Air New Zealand spokesman Cameron Hill told Reuters he understood due diligence had been carried out on Jetset.

He declined to comment specifically but said: "Up to now we haven't been necessarily a ready seller, but circumstances have changed. Jetset are now heading off into technological developments that we don't believe are part of our core business and, through our new investment in Ansett, we have a connection to a distribution facility within Australia."
Asked if Jetset had become surplus to requirements, Hill replied: "Well that's the conclusion you're drawing."
Speaking about Jetset chairman and managing director Isi Leibler's option to acquire Air NZ's stake in the group, Hill said: "He's always had pre-emptive rights, as with any joint venture."
